title: MetaExtractor review verdict file
description: What one reviewer returned for one draft. Pinned to the draft by SHA-256: a verdict file is only meaningful against the exact extraction it was formed on, so `draft_sha256` must match the draft the packet was built from. Reviewer verdicts are never mixed with the held-out gold.

draft_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the ExtractionResult the packet was built from. `review ingest` refuses a verdict file whose pin does not match.

paper_id.description: Identifier of the reviewed study, as recorded on the draft.

mode.description: Which kind of packet produced this. `draft` = every extracted value is a unit, no gold involved. `adjudication` = sampled scored cells judged against the source, for studies that have gold.

reviewer.description: Who reviewed. Free-form but stable, since inter-reviewer agreement is computed across files.

notes.description: Anything the reviewer wants to say about the draft as a whole.

verdicts.description: One entry per unit the reviewer judged. Units left unjudged are simply absent; the report counts them as such rather than assuming agreement.

unit_id.description: Stable identity of the unit, as emitted by the packet builder: `field:<name>` for a study-level value, `sample:<index>:<field>` for a sample cell, `cell:<sample_idx>:<field>` for an adjudication unit.

verdict.description: `supported` = the source bears out the extracted value. `unsupported` = it does not. `wrong_value` = the field is right to report but the value is wrong. `cannot_determine` = the evidence available to the reviewer does not settle it (the honest answer when a value lives in a supplement that retrieval never fetched). `gold_wrong` = adjudication only: the extraction is right and the curated value is not.

corrected_value.description: What the reviewer believes the value should be, when they can say.
